dimensions.label: Specificity
dimensions.question: How specific are the words in `hook.text`? Count concrete details a viewer could picture or check.
levels: Generic: could run for any company (like "Quality work you can trust"); no number, place, person, problem or result named.
Mostly generic: names a room, a service or an audience, but nothing a viewer could picture or check.
One concrete detail (a place, a number, a named problem or a clear result); the rest is general.
Two or more concrete details, like a place and a number, or a named problem and a timeline.
Concrete all the way through: exact numbers or timelines, a named person or place and a result a viewer could picture or check.

dimensions.label: Avatar match
dimensions.question: How clearly is `hook.text` written for ONE person in `avatars`? Check two things: does it say WHO they are, and does it name THEIR exact problem or situation?
levels: Written for nobody in particular, or about the company itself ("We are...", "Our team...").
Written for everyone ("householders", "business owners"): no situation or problem that belongs to one person in `avatars`.
Fits the situation of one person in `avatars` in general words, but names neither who they are nor their exact problem.
Names the exact problem or situation of one person in `avatars` (their pain, in words they would use), but not who they are.
Names who they are AND their exact problem, in words they would use, for one person in `avatars` only.

dimensions.label: Curiosity gap
dimensions.question: How strongly does `hook.text` make the viewer want to see what comes next?
levels: Nothing to find out: a plain statement, label or slogan that closes itself.
Mild: a topic is raised, but the answer is obvious or already given in the same line.
A clear question or tease, but a familiar one the viewer has seen many times.
An open loop: sets up a specific mistake, surprise, reveal or result and holds back the payoff.
A strong open loop: a specific, unexpected or slightly uncomfortable setup the viewer can only settle by watching or clicking.

dimensions.label: Offer clarity
dimensions.question: How clearly does `hook.text` say what the viewer gets if they act, and what to do next?
levels: No offer: nothing the viewer gets and nothing to do.
An offer is only implied ("we can help", "find out how"), with nothing concrete to get.
Names what they get in general words (a quote, a consultation, a renovation), with no detail about it.
A concrete offer with a detail that makes it easy to say yes: free, local, vetted, no pressure or a timeline.
A concrete offer plus the next step in plain words: exactly what they get, what it costs them (like free) and what to do now.

dimensions.label: Visual stop power
dimensions.question: How strongly would the first 3 seconds of this video stop someone scrolling? Judge `video.first_3_seconds` and `video.on_screen_text`.
levels: Nothing stands out in the first 3 seconds: a logo, a dark or blank frame, or a slow establishing shot.
A plain shot of a room or a person with little movement and no on-screen text.
A clear subject (a person talking or a room) with some movement or on-screen text, but nothing unusual.
A striking opening: a big reveal, a strong before, bold on-screen text or a person speaking straight to the camera from the first frame.
An opening nobody could miss: a dramatic transformation or surprising image together with bold text in the first second.

dimensions.label: Brand fit
dimensions.question: Does `hook.text` follow this channel's voice and rules? Check it against `channel.brief` and every line of `channel.notes`.
levels: Breaks a rule: names someone `channel.notes` says never to name, makes a claim `channel.notes` does not allow, or speaks as the wrong speaker.
Off voice: hype, shouting, fake urgency or corporate phrases ("we pride ourselves"), or it is about the company instead of the viewer.
Breaks no rule but has no voice: a bare label, slogan or list of services (like "Garden, Deck, or Both").
On voice: plain words about the viewer's own room, problem or goal, calm and confident, and every claim is one `channel.notes` allows.
On voice and tied to this channel: plain words about the viewer plus a detail from `channel.notes` (a place, a product or a proof point) used the way `channel.notes` allows.

mechanics.label: Be specific
mechanics.definition: Exact details carry it: a precise person, number, place or real result instead of general words.

mechanics.label: Lead with a number
mechanics.definition: Opens with a number that carries time, effort or cost, like "in 1 week", "under $5" or "10 years".

mechanics.label: Call out the audience
mechanics.definition: Names who it is for so they pick themselves out, like "New householders:" or "Installers,".

mechanics.label: Lean into the taboo
mechanics.definition: Says what competitors are too polite to say out loud.

mechanics.label: Primal desire
mechanics.definition: Sells a deep want (status, safety, belonging, approval, pride) instead of a product feature.

mechanics.label: Curiosity loop
mechanics.definition: Shows the setup and hides the payoff behind the click.

mechanics.label: Negative
mechanics.definition: Phrased in the negative: names what the viewer fears, hates or wants to avoid.

mechanics.label: Golden nugget testimonial
mechanics.definition: Borrows a real customer's own words.

mechanics.label: Show the transformation
mechanics.definition: Puts the before and the after in front of the viewer instead of describing the result.

mechanics.label: None
mechanics.definition: None of these: a plain statement, slogan or label.

seed.rtmNotes:
Northstar Media is Alex Nolan's one person marketing brand: Meta ads, plus the landing page and the automated follow up behind them.
Audience: small business owners who need ad spend to turn into booked calls, leads and sales. Home services businesses are the specialty and the proof.
Working line (the site headline): "Meta ads that turn ad spend into booked calls."
Channel lanes: the site, YouTube, Reels and social speak to small business owners in general with home services as proof; cold email speaks to home services trades only.
Why Alex over an agency: the person in the ad account every day is the person on the sales call. No account managers, no team relaying notes.
Alex never handles a client's lead intake or calls: never promise call handling, call backs or appointment setting by Alex.
The number that matters is the conversion the business gets paid on (booked appointments for service businesses); cost per lead is reported weekly in plain English.
Voice: first person singular ("I build", "I run"), plain, casual, confident and specific; honest even when it costs; never talks down to owners.
Hard copy rules: no dashes as punctuation and no hyphenated compound words (write "follow up", "done for you"); no AI tell phrases; no US state names or abbreviations.
Never name a client or any of Alex's other companies; proof is anonymized ("a garden and deck renovator").
Never state a price, a price range or a pricing structure. Only cost per lead, only with its date window, never cost per appointment.
Recurring lines: "Ad. Page. Booked." and "I run this playbook on my own businesses first."
seed.whosWho:
Riley is the face and voice of SGD Pros: a man in a black t-shirt (usually with green shorts), filmed talking to the camera in a modern garden with mint green cabinets and white countertops.
The Intro and Outro folders are his filmed lines. A description of that man in that garden is Riley.
Alex (Alex N) is the face of Northstar Media: his own YouTube episodes, thumbnails and reels.
Morgan (Morgan Price, Alex's partner) is a face of SGD (Summit Gardens and Decks): the Morgan Ads folders are his filmed videos; Riley appears in SGD's Riley Ads folders too.
seed.companyNotes:
Summit Gardens and Decks (SGD) is Alex's own renovation company and speaks as itself (we, our team), plain and direct, never as a connector or directory.
Faces: Morgan (Morgan Price, Alex's partner) in the Morgan Ads videos and Riley in the Riley Ads videos; both may speak on camera by first name.
Service area: New Jersey and Pennsylvania; the Meta ads target affluent ZIP codes in Eastby, Unity, Morrow, Summerset, Midby and Maple counties, New Jersey.
Services: full garden and deck renovations, managed by one team from design through construction; no small repairs or partial updates.
How it works: a free walkthrough at the home, then a clear scope and price, then one team schedules and runs the project start to finish, so the householder never juggles multiple installers.
Next step in the ads: a free consultation or free walkthrough, booked through summitgardens.example.
What works: Morgan's own videos of real SGD projects carry the live ads, and "Dream Gardens Start Here" gets nearly all headline delivery; strong angles are no juggling installers, one team from design to construction, a before and after reveal of a real SGD garden, and a simple three step process.
Audience: householders in affluent New Jersey suburbs, mostly women (about 7 in 10 leads), ages 25 and up.
Proof allowed: 8+ years of renovation experience, and before and after photos or video of SGD's own projects.
Claims not allowed: 10+ years (use 8+), dollar prices or price ranges, financing or payment plans, a count of jobs done, reviews, ratings or testimonials presented as SGD's own (the website reviews belong to the parent company, Summit Home Buyers).
seed.companyHint: Summit Gardens and Decks (SGD): Alex's own company doing full garden and deck renovations, design through construction, in New Jersey (Eastby, Unity, Morrow, Summerset, Midby, Maple counties) and Pennsylvania.

brandNotes.acme:
Sells full garden renovations, full deck renovations and whole home renovations, with one team from start to finish.
Where: Maple County, New Jersey (Reed Bank, Rowan, Midvale, Fenton Falls, Fairhold, Holbrook, Colt Ridge, Long Reach, Ashby Park). Ads may say New Jersey or Maple County. Anything outside Maple County is out.
Claims allowed: free consultation, free walkthrough, free quote, honest pricing up front, no pressure, one team start to finish, garden, deck or both.
Gardens take months (cabinets about 8 to 10 weeks from order, then 12 to 15 weeks to finish). Never promise a fast garden or a timeline in days or weeks.
Claims not allowed: any price, monthly payment or financing; licensed or insured; star ratings or review counts; a number of years in business (his founding year is unconfirmed).
Do not add new experience or volume claims. The launch lines about a decade of work and hundreds of New Jersey gardens describe local pros in general, not his own record.
A generated room image may only be a labeled before or design rendering, never his finished work. Never say our work, our crews or recent project.
Never use footage or copy that says New York. This is a New Jersey client.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which connects the householder with a vetted local pro. Never speak as Adam or Acme Restoration, and never name them.
brandNotes.bluebird:
Sells garden and deck renovations, mostly in older Eastport homes and brownstones. Ads lean to gardens (about 2 to 3 gardens a month versus about 1 deck).
Also does brownstone molding and plaster restoration, custom carpentry and full gut renovations. Whole home work appears in two launch ads, but lead with gardens and decks.
Where: Eastport (Prospect Gardens, Eastport Heights, Park Hill, Bedford Row) and Southeast Kingsport (St. Albion, Laurelby, Kingsport Village, Cambry Heights, Hollow). Eastport copy and Kingsport copy are separate, each for its own ad set.
Claims allowed: decades of carpentry and renovation experience (over twenty years), the team pulls its own permits, a one year warranty on their labor, prewar and brownstone experience.
Offer wording allowed: free in home walkthrough, honest numbers, no pressure, no obligation.
Claims not allowed: any price, monthly payment or financing; licensed, insured or bonded (the license on file shows inactive); a founding year.
Visuals are her own real Eastport job photos. Never present a generated room as her finished work.
Never name Bluebird Carpentry, Dee, Toby or the Bell family in any ad, spoken or written.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which matches the householder with a trusted Eastport or Kingsport team. Never speak as Bluebird Carpentry or use their name as the speaker.
brandNotes.cedar:
Sells garden cabinet refinishing: new doors, drawer fronts and finishes on the existing cabinet boxes, plus new countertops (quartz). No full garden renovations, no decks.
Where: Centerville, Kingsport, Eastport and Shoreham County. Copy says local or New York, never Lakeside or upstate.
Claims allowed: installed in as little as 3 days (or usually about 3 days), same layout, no demolition, no weeks of mess, a fraction of the cost of new cabinets.
Claims allowed: hundreds of gardens refinished, neat and on time crews, finishes that last, free in home quote, no obligation.
Price anchor: as little as $99/month, only as a from price, once per text, and never in both the headline and the primary text of one ad.
Beat any competitor's price is allowed only on the $99/month financing angle.
Claims not allowed: a flat only $99 a month, licensed or insured, star ratings or review counts, years in business, anything about decks or gut renovations.
Never name Cedar Direct, CDX, Ben or Brandt, and never mix in facts from the Lakeside refinishing client.
Ads run on Instagram Reels only, so the primary text carries the message and the headline may not show.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which matches the householder with a trusted local refinishing team. Never speak as Cedar Direct or Ben.
brandNotes.delta:
Sells full garden renovations and full deck renovations. They lead with decks; master decks with custom tile and double vanities are their stated specialty.
Where: South Jersey, 22 ZIPs in Camber, Burlton and Glouton counties. Geo words: South Jersey and Cherry Vale area. No other town names, and never Merrin or Atlas county.
Claims allowed: BBB accredited with an A plus rating, NARI member, renovation South Jersey homes since 2020, rated 5.0 on Google (never paired with a review or project count).
Claims allowed from their reviews: a crew that shows up, communicates, keeps the schedule, respects the home, cleans up and sweats the details; weeks, not months; real before and after photos of their own jobs.
Claims not allowed: any price, financing, monthly payments or payment plans (they offer none); licensed or insured; 450+ projects, 98% satisfaction or 20+ years; any warranty; one day or fixed day completion.
No windows, doors, basements, decks, siding, roofing or whole house work, even though they sell it. One room and one person per ad.
Never present a mid construction photo as a finished room.
Never name Coral, Sand, Yuri, Glen or Jared.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which matches the householder with a trusted South Jersey team. Never speak as Coral Renovation or use their name as the speaker.
brandNotes.everest:
Sells garden cabinet refinishing: the cabinet boxes stay, the doors, drawer fronts and finishes are replaced, with an optional new laminate countertop.
Countertops are laminate only. Never say quartz or granite.
Where: the Lakeside area (a 52 ZIP Lakeside group across Munro, Orland and nearby counties). Geo word is Lakeside. Bufford is in their territory but not in the ads.
Claims allowed: most gardens done in about 3 days, days not months, no demolition, same layout, boxes stay, Lakeside householders have chosen refinishing for years, trusted Lakeside crews.
Offer wording allowed: free in person quote, no obligation.
Claims not allowed: any price, the $99/month offer, any financing, any tax mention, licensed or insured, star ratings, years in business.
Garden refinishing only in ads: no full garden renovations, no decks.
Never name Cedar Direct, CDX, Eli, Elias, Hale or Finn, and never borrow facts or offers from the New York City refinishing client.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which connects the householder with a trusted Lakeside refinishing team. Never speak as Cedar Direct or as Eli and Finn.
brandNotes.fairway:
Sells full deck and full garden renovations in three tiers (Essential, Preferred, Signature), including co-op and condo work. Quotes are all in: labor, materials, project management and design.
Does not do cabinet refinishing. Never run a refinishing angle for this client.
Where: Eastport and Kingsport (Astor, East Elmfield, Forest Glen, Bayview, Fresh Fields, Riverside, Greenhaven, Park Hill, Bay Crest, Bedford Row, Prospect Rise, Clinton Rise, Fort Green). Geo word is New York; copy stays borough neutral.
Claims allowed: licensed (the word only, never the license number), co-op and condo renovation experience, free in home consultation or free quote, clear pricing up front, one team start to finish, no pressure.
Deck copy may name walk in showers, heated floors and finishes that last (the approved spa angle).
Claims not allowed: any price or tier band, financing, years in business (the company formed in 2026), star ratings or review counts, MWBE, an office address, hundreds of times.
Never name Fairway Home Pros, FWHP or Fay Gomez.
Voice: connector voice. Ads run as SGD Pros, which connects New York householders with a trusted, licensed local team. Never speak as Fairway Home Pros or Fay.
brandNotes.granite:
Sells single deck renovations only, as two different products: the One Week Deck System (prefab acrylic or solid surface wall panels) and Custom Tile decks. Also tub to shower conversions.
The panel system is not tile. Never call it tile, tile look or grout. The about a week and matter of days claims belong to the panel system and tub to shower conversions only, never a custom tile deck.
Where: North Jersey, about 125 towns in Morrow, Berwyn, Passmore, Southby, Eastby, Wardell, Unity and Summerset counties. Geo word is North Jersey, never a single county.
Claims allowed: family owned since 1983 (over four decades), most decks renovated in about a week (panel system), old tub to walk in shower in a matter of days, licensed, factory certified employees, award winning.
Claims allowed: hundreds of reviews (4.9 stars only in written copy), walk in showers with a low threshold, built in seating and grab bars, free in home quote.
